1.22 Boundaries of this release

  • Comparison discovery is DNG-specific and name-based; it is not a universal RAW-to-DNG conversion matcher or an automatic renamed-photo detector.
  • Selected TIFF page order and tags define the stored-sample scope. Unsupported layouts and codec failures stay unverified.
  • Equal stored samples do not mean equal renderings, edits or cloud records.
  • No Lightroom catalog, native digest registration, Sync queue or cloud payload is modified.
  • ExifTool-visible fields do not cover every private/unparsed byte. Whole-file recovery covers payload bytes when metadata reports cannot explain them.
  • Rust and Python caches are filesystem-identity reuse, not an always-fresh cryptographic reread; their identity policies differ deliberately.
  • Some low-level tools depend on exclusive ownership by their caller. In particular, Rust report directories are not automatically locked, and Rust metadata batches need an unchanged input pair set and source scope.
  • Byte archives can depend on immutable reference copies. Full-copy mode avoids that dependency at the cost of storage.
  • A complete report describes the declared inventory and direction. It does not certify unrelated folders, public cloud convergence or deletion eligibility.

The useful result is an explainable archive decision: what matches, what differs, what remains unverified, and exactly how a retained original can be reconstructed.
